title: Stretchy cast-off for lace
subtitle: A yarn-over cast-off that keeps lace edges open and flat.
excerpt: The stretchy cast-off inserts a yarn over between each cast-off stitch, producing an edge that opens fully when blocked and does not pull in under tension.
sourceNotes: Technique in common use for lace finishing. Yarn-over cast-off mechanics documented across British lace knitting traditions. See also Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) chapter on finishing lace.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cast-off variant that places a yarn over between each pair of stitches before passing them over, creating extra length in the cast-off chain so the edge stretches to match the lace body when blocked.

content.text: A standard cast-off on a lace edge grips the last row and prevents the piece from opening to its full width when blocked. The

places a yarn over between each cast-off stitch, adding extra length to the chain so the edge can open fully under blocking tension. The result is a cast-off edge that disappears into the points of the lace rather than pulling them down. Difficulty: intermediate, because the yarn-over rhythm needs to be consistent.
4 mm needles (or the size called for by your pattern)
Knit the first stitch onto the right needle.
Yarn over (bring the yarn over the right needle from front to back).
Knit the next stitch. Three loops are on the right needle: the original stitch, the yarn over, and the new stitch.
Pass the original stitch (the leftmost) over the yarn over. Two loops remain.
Pass the yarn over over the new stitch. One loop remains: the new stitch, which is now the starting stitch for the next repeat.
Repeat steps 2-5 across the row. Fasten off the last stitch as normal.

Any lace shawl or stole with a pointed or scalloped cast-off edge benefits from the stretchy variant. When in doubt on a lace piece, cast off with this method rather than the standard one; the piece can always be tightened by using a smaller needle for the cast-off row, but it cannot be loosened after the fact.

items.symptom: Edge still pulls in after blocking
items.cause: Yarn-overs worked too tightly, or needle size too small
items.fix: Try using a needle two sizes larger for the cast-off row, keeping the yarn-over loose.

items.cause: Yarn-overs too loose, or needle size too large
items.fix: Use a needle only one size larger than the body, and work the yarn-overs at body tension.

items.symptom: Lost track of which stitch to pass over
items.fix: Work very slowly for the first 10 stitches, naming each loop aloud: 'stitch, yarn over, new stitch; pass stitch over yarn over; pass yarn over over new stitch'.
